Name: Forest for All NYC (coalition)
What they do: Coalition for a healthy, equitable urban forest; 200+ members, convened by The Nature Conservancy. Runs the annual City of Forest Day (Oct 2026).
Why relevant for EcoScape: One door to many planting and stewardship groups; already working on the NYC Urban Forest Plan (Local Law 148).

Name: Trees New York
What they do: Citizen Pruner training (licensed by NYC Parks), youth environmental education, school and neighbourhood tree plantings. Active 2026 (Trees for NYCHA, Cooling the Campus).
Why relevant for EcoScape: Teaches tree care: our 'learn to maintain' module mirrors its mission. Has a corporate sponsorship and volunteering offer.
Possible role: Planter, educational content, stewardship of plantings

Name: New York Restoration Project (NYRP)
What they do: Free tree giveaways with community partners since 2008: 3,750 trees distributed 4 Apr–16 May 2026, over 80,500 in total. Also community gardens and park restoration.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Direct channel to distribute and plant real trees with residents; already funded by Bloomberg Philanthropies.

Name: NYC Parks — Street Tree Planting / Forestry
What they do: Plants and maintains street trees; Neighborhood Tree Planting Program prioritises heat-vulnerable areas. Note: an Oct 2026 Council op-ed says individual tree requests are no longer accepted, while the official page still invites 311 requests.
Why relevant for EcoScape: The authority for any street tree in NYC; publishes the tree data we use. (MillionTreesNYC was completed in 2015 per NYRP; its old domain now redirects to an unrelated site: do not cite it.)

Name: NYC Parks GreenThumb
What they do: Supports 550+ community gardens with free materials, technical help and workshops; active 2026-27 programme guides.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Best fit for the edible-garden and pollinator options in NYC.

Name: BetaNYC
What they do: Helps New Yorkers use open data and technology: RADAR data help desk, NYC School of Data, BetaBagels. Active Oct 2026.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Credibility on open data; NYC School of Data 2027 call for proposals (deadline 6 Dec 2026) is a stage to present the prototype.

Name: The Nature Conservancy — New York (Future Forest NYC)
What they do: Future Forest NYC (since 2019): science on canopy, convenes Forest for All NYC, engages New Yorkers in tree care.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Source of canopy science and 'practical canopy' analysis to choose where to plant.

Name: Bloomberg Philanthropies
What they do: Large philanthropy active on cities and climate; thanked by NYRP for supporting its tree stewardship work (2026).
Why relevant for EcoScape: Flagship climate and cities funder named in the brief; credibility if even a small grant or mention.

Name: NYC Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC)
What they do: Climate innovation programmes; BATWorks climate innovation hub at Brooklyn Army Terminal (opening expected 2028); 'Pilots at BAT' programme led by LACI from 2026.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Possible pilot channel for climate-tech startups; mentioned in the brief.

Name: Brooklyn Grange (+ City Growers)
What they do: Rooftop farms in NYC; partner non-profit City Growers runs farm-based K-12 education on its roofs; hosts corporate events.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Showcase for edible urban planting; possible corporate-event venue for sponsor activations.

Name: NYC Open Data (Office of Technology and Innovation)
What they do: Publishes Street Tree Census, Forestry Tree Points and Heat Vulnerability Index.
Why relevant for EcoScape: Core data source for the NYC version of the map.
